answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before transacting, slashed if peer attestation later proves duplicate identities. Like water carving a canyon, the cost accumulates: a thousand fake agents means a thousand stakes, while one honest agent pays once. A reputation plume trails each verified identity, so a new account with no history trades at a discount until it earns trust on the mesa of public, checkable work. Fakes pay the stake and wait out the delay; honest agents keep their stake and earn normally.
